dse_runs.notes: Bursty spec: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 latency <= 0.4 us. A single iterative CORDIC (12 iters, ~12 cycles @ 150 MHz = 80 ns) cannot drain an 8-deep burst before the next burst arrives (avg 0.5 us apart) — expect queue buildup and p99 violation. Prior campaigns: iterative family reached the front; pipelined/unrolled_k/pipelined_m never did on this device, but this spec's latency constraint may favor pipelined (1-cycle latency, throughput-limited) designs. Prior area-min winner: iterative dw=16, n_iter=12, truncation (267 LUTs+FFs, 10.5 acc bits). Selection rule: min luts_plus_ffs among feasible.

final_text:
Campaign complete — all specs finalized.

**Summary:** The single spec `bursty_offload` (8-channel sensor front end, bursts of 8 requests, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 latency ≤ 0.4 us, min LUTs+FFs) was taken down the full ladder. L1 (`run_dse`, all 400 evals) mapped a 38-design feasible Pareto front; the bursty latency constraint pushed the front toward pipelined_m designs (which, unlike prior campaigns, reached the front here). L2 SimPy simulation confirmed the top-5 all pass — the L1 analytic p99 bound was optimistic (0.168 → simulated 0.233 us) but comfortably under 0.4 us. L3/L4/L5 returned no recorded measured data for this design class (no L3 row, no L4 synthesis), so back_annotate found nothing to compare and no winner change was flagged. Final selection: **pipelined_m, data_width=15, n_iter=14, m=7** — 855 LUTs+FFs (estimate), 10.6 accuracy bits, 59.6 MSPS throughput, max error 2^-10.63, simulated p99 latency 0.233 us.
